about.ogTitle: About Sentiment Inside Out - Market Sentiment Analysis Platform
about.heading: About Sentiment Inside Out
about.section1Text: This is a famous quote from André Kostolany, author of 'The Speculator's Confession'. Funds = Fundamentals = Macroeconomics. Psychology = Investor Sentiment = Human Nature. I believe cycles stem from human irrationality, creating the peaks and troughs of the economy and stock market.
about.section2Text: Economic data and company reports change monthly or quarterly, yet the capital market can fluctuate dramatically in short periods. This shows that sentiment's impact on price is no less than fundamentals. Some sell fearing it's too expensive; others buy fearing they'll miss out. As market participants, we should understand whether the market is currently in a state of fear or greed.
about.section3Text: I believe stock prices reflect market sentiment just as much as fundamentals. The website was founded with the goal of using simple charts and data to transform current market sentiment into important investment indicators, helping everyone overcome their irrationality and avoid chasing highs and selling lows based on emotion.

current.title: About the SIO Fear & Greed Indicator
current.subtitle: It helps investors step back from subjective emotion and judge market risk appetite more objectively.

section1.title: 1. It combines multiple indicators
section1.body: SIO brings retail sentiment, options hedging, volatility pressure, capital flows, credit spreads, and institutional and active-manager positioning into one framework, then converts them into a 0 to 100 score. The {{score}} reading you see now is the combined output of those signals.

section2.title: 2. Spot extremes instead of chasing the short term
section2.body: When the score falls into very low territory, fear is usually spreading. When it rises into very high territory, the market may already be overheating. The key is to watch whether conditions are moving toward a more extreme reading.

section3.title: 3. Read the market with discipline and resist fear and greed
section3.body: When markets fall hard, people instinctively want to get out. When markets surge, FOMO makes it easy to chase. SIO adds an objective, cross-indicator reference point to your decision-making.

priceAnalysis.pageDescription: The LOHAS five-line chart fits a trend line to a stock and marks how far today’s price sits from it — from extreme fear to extreme greed. Pick a span of 0.5, 1.5 or 3.5 years. The LOHAS Channel then shows whether price has left the range it recently traded in.
priceAnalysis.keywords: LOHAS Five-Line Analysis, Price Trend Analysis, Stock Analysis, Market Sentiment, Mean Reversion, Overbought Oversold, LOHAS Channel, Standard Deviation

jsonLd.name: LOHAS Five-Line Analysis
jsonLd.description: The LOHAS Five-Line fits a trend to the last 3.5 years of prices and adds two lines either side, marking how far price usually strays from that trend. The closer to the outer edge, the further price sits from its long-term trend: the top line shows as "Extreme Greed", the bottom as "Extreme Fear". Read alongside the faster-moving LOHAS Channel, it indicates whether the short term is overheated or oversold. It is a way to see where a stock or index ETF sits in its long-term trend — a reference point, not a standalone basis for buying or selling.

fearOnly.title: Extreme Fear, but still inside the channel

greedConfirmed.title: Extreme Greed + Above the upper edge
greedConfirmed.body: Extreme Greed coincides with a break above the channel. Watch for price to return inside. Backtested across 43 index ETFs, selling on that return avoided 1.7 percentage points more of the following month’s decline than random selling.

greedOnly.title: Extreme Greed, but still inside the channel
greedOnly.body: The five-line chart shows Extreme Greed while price stays inside the channel. The trend may continue, but holding time matters: backtested across 43 index ETFs, one-year returns trailed random entry by 3.6 percentage points.

sentimentBoard.divergenceNote: Retail surveys, institutional positioning and different markets often read the same moment differently. The larger the gap, the wider the disagreement. Retail comes from the AAII survey; institutional from NAAIM exposure, COT and the junk bond spread.

divergences.cnn_vs_sio: CNN Fear & Greed vs SIO US Fear & Greed

external.title: Widely watched sentiment indicators
external.note: Sentiment gauges published by other institutions. CNN Fear & Greed reacts quickly but runs short-term, often reaching extreme fear well before prices bottom. The BofA Bull & Bear Indicator updates weekly, and the underlying report is not public.

us.title: US sentiment indicators
us.note: AAII retail surveys, NAAIM manager exposure, options Put/Call and credit spreads are among the signals behind the SIO US Fear & Greed Index.

tw.title: Taiwan sentiment indicators
tw.note: Taiwan index options volatility, foreign institutional futures positioning and margin maintenance ratios are among the signals behind the SIO Taiwan Fear & Greed Index. Taiwan's positioning structure differs from the US, so the two indices use separate indicator sets.
